notes:
CRM notes / call snippets:
- Use case: real-time vessel telemetry enrichment + operator chat. Heavy embeddings index for historical tracks + reranking on anomaly detections. Need deterministic latency during port maneuvers.
- Throughput / capacity ask: baseline 500 RPS sustained for short multi-tenant bursts, ability to burst to 1k RPS for 30m windows. Planning reserved GPU pool: initial 4xA100-equivalent GPUs, ability to scale to 8 during peak season.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 60ms (short responses), p99 < 120ms for up to 1k-token generation (mostly short, occasional long summaries). Pelorus expects routing to low-latency hosts for live ops.
- Uptime and credits: Pelorus pushing for 99.95% uptime SLA. Proposed credit schedule (from Pelorus procurement): 5% monthly credit for each 0.1% below 99.95% down to 99.5%, 10% credit below 99.5% — Redwood asked for capped liability and operational exclusions. Legal needs concrete wording.
- Maintenance windows: Pelorus operations run 24/7; prefers maintenance windows Sundays 02:00-05:00 UTC only, and no maintenance during scheduled port operations (client will provide blackout calendar). They ask for advance 21 days notice for any non-emergency maintenance. Redwood proposed rolling patch strategy with <5 minute instance impact.
- Support / response times: CTO asked for P1 phone escalation + 1 hour initial response SLA, on-call SE engagement within 2 hours, P2 within 4 hours. Pelorus requires clear escalation path to account-level engineering and monthly incident reviews.
- Fallback / graceful degradation: must support automatic fallback to a smaller model variant (quantized) with preserved prefix caching to avoid total outage for operator workflows. Pelorus wants routing policy to keep critical routes on dedicated pool.
- Data & compliance: data residency requirement for EU-regional datasets (must stay in eu region), full audit logs retention 13 months, KMS integration for keys.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high cost tolerance if strict SLO + reserved capacity guarantees; prefers predictable monthly committed spend vs variable bursts.
- Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-18): "We cannot accept silent 5+ minute outages during berth operations — it's a safety issue."
- Open items for Redwood: provide explicit credit schedule language for SLA, confirm maintenance blackout enforcement, finalize GPU reservation sizing and burst policy, produce POC runbook and measurement script for p99 latency verification.
- Stubs/links: pricing deck (drive://redwood/pelorus/pricing-v2), security FAQ (drive://redwood/pelorus/security-faq), Fireflies notes (ff_2026-02-03_8921).
- Sales tact: push Dedicated with 12-month commit + 3-month POC; emphasize Optimize recommendations to reduce required GPUs via batching/kv-cache.
procurement_notes: Legal asked for: indemnity cap, force majeure carveouts for cloud provider outages, and 30-day SLA termination right if credits exceed threshold. Finance asked for net-60 payment terms but willing to do net-30 for annual commit.
technical_requirements_summary: Reserved pool of GPUs (4x) with autoscaling to burst to 8 for 30m windows; p99 latency verification scripts required as part of acceptance; per-route routing policy to lock critical routes to dedicated pool; KV prefix caching and continuous batching enabled; metrics exported to customer's Prometheus endpoint for observability.
